key_insight: Dynamic replanning creates a security gap in multi-agent AI: a malicious agent can hide instructions in its feedback and steer the orchestrator’s next plan. Kaer targets this replanning vulnerability.
problem_solved: Protecting an orchestrator from agent feedback that attempts to hijack plan revisions—a risk not fully addressed by per-tool access controls or static, pre-execution policies.
method: Focus security analysis on the feedback-to-replanning boundary, where agent outputs can influence future actions.
Address security during plan revision rather than relying solely on initial-plan checks or tool permissions.
The supplied abstract is truncated, so Kaer’s specific mechanisms and evaluation results cannot be confirmed.
impact: Practitioners should treat agent feedback as untrusted input, especially when it can reshape workflows. The paper highlights why security controls must account for changing plans, not just individual tool calls.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: orchestrator → agents → feedback → revised plan.
Attack overlay showing malicious instructions entering through agent feedback.
Comparison graphic contrasting static checks and tool permissions with replanning-time security.
Trust-boundary icon separating agent-provided content from orchestrator instructions.
paper_title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems
paper_authors: Tushin Mallick, Evan Rose, Matthew Laws, Alina Oprea, Cristina Nita-Rotaru
